title: GUI process execution and cancellation lifecycle
overview: Ensure commands launched by the OneFLOW GUI have bounded process-tree cancellation, direct-child reaping, output-pipe completion, and an explicit task outcome.
principle: A task owns the process it starts and must not report final completion while its direct child remains unreaped or its output reader is still active. Cancellation is a lifecycle transition, not merely a request to terminate the root PID. Platform-specific process-tree operations belong at the process-control boundary; task-specific result semantics remain with each runner.
architecture: The GUI test worker, Case Database runner, and workflow process runner create isolated process groups and delegate shutdown to process_control. terminate_and_reap applies a shared escalation policy. Each caller retains ownership of its output forwarding and typed result. This contract is separate from the accelerator runtime lifecycle contract: it governs operating-system processes launched by the desktop workbench, not backend resource finalization inside the solver.

verification.scope: tools/oneflow_gui/test_process_control.py; verifies the normal tree-termination and direct-child wait sequence.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_process_control.py; verifies retry after the initial wait timeout.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_process_control.py; verifies direct-child kill and reap as the final fallback.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_runner_process.py; verifies Case Database runner cancellation removes solver descendants.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_workflow_process.py; verifies workflow cancellation removes external-process descendants.

proves: The three GUI process execution paths use a shared process-tree termination and direct-child reaping policy.
The process-control unit tests cover normal shutdown, timeout escalation, and a direct-child fallback.
Native descendant tests are declared for POSIX and Windows, with execution dependent on the host platform.
does_not_prove: That every MPI implementation terminates all remote ranks or launcher-managed processes.
That cancellation can interrupt a process stuck in an uninterruptible kernel or driver state.
That GUI task results are durably persisted across application restarts.
That every caller waits for every output-reader thread under all possible I/O failures.
That solver numerical results are correct.
